title: AI will create jobs, U.S. CEOs say in KPMG survey
key_facts: KPMG US released a survey on Thursday (15 Oct 2026) of 400 CEOs of major US-based companies.
About nine out of ten CEOs expect to increase head count over the next three years.
Three-quarters said AI integration made them reassess skills required for entry-level roles.
About four in ten said AI agents delivered significant efficiency or growth gains; only 9% called agents transformational today.
More than eight in ten call AI a top investment priority for the next three years.
Tim Walsh, CEO and chair of KPMG US, said humans are still needed to review agents' work.
quote_evidence: About nine out of 10 chiefs said they expected to increase head count over the next three years.
Three-quarters said that the integration of AI systems had made them reassess the skills required for entry-level roles.
Yet only 9% described agents, which are designed to carry out tasks, as "transformational" for their organizations today.
why_it_matters_hint: Big US bosses say they plan to hire more, not fewer, people despite AI.
